source.title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions

accepted.question_text: For a string propagating on three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space with an NS–NS two-form, so that the worldsheet sigma model is the SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten model, how can one construct a complete perturbative spectrum of physical string states that is consistent with the basic requirements of string theory and conformal field theory?

evidence.quote: Despite the progress made in various directions, several quite elementary questions remain unanswered, in particular in the very simple case of three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space.

I will very briefly review these problems, discuss in some detail the important issue of constructing a consistent spectrum for a string propagating on ADS3 plus torsion background, and comment on potential solutions.

As far as string theory is concerned, ADS3 is an exact background, provided an NS–NS two-form is switched on. In fact, three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space is the universal covering of the SU(1,1) group manifold, and the corresponding two-dimensional conformally invariant sigma model is a Wess–Zumino–Witten model.
No satisfactory understanding of its basic features, such as the complete spectrum of perturbative states, has yet been reached.

accepted.question_text: What is the exact structure of the fundamental string theory on an anti-de Sitter background, and how does that exact string theory connect to the super-Yang–Mills or boundary conformal field theory expected from the AdS/CFT correspondence, including the computation of AdS3 string-state correlators needed for rigorous checks?
accepted.context_brief: exact AdS string theory and AdS/CFT checks

evidence.quote: Since the supergravity theory under consideration is the low-energy limit of a more fundamental superstring theory, the question arises of the exact structure of the latter on the anti-de Sitter background, and its connexion to the super-Yang–Mills theory on the boundary.
Ideally, we would like to compute correlators in both sides and compare them. In practice, correlators for ADS3 string states are out of reach, which makes any rigorous check quite intricate.
as long as one does not handle the ADS3 side exactly, the achievements are limited both on checking the ADS/CFT correspondence, and on building the boundary theory.

accepted.question_text: In the SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten conformal field theory, how should highest-weight current-algebra representations based on the discrete series and the continuous series be combined into a consistent, possibly non-unitary model whose operator product algebra and genus-one partition function satisfy modular invariance?
accepted.context_brief: SU(1,1) WZW representation content and modular invariance

evidence.quote: Irreducible representations of the global algebra are essentially of two kinds: discrete D∓(j) or continuous principal Cp(b,a) and continuous supplementary Cs(j,a).
I now come to the following crucial question: How should the above representations be combined to form a consistent, though non-unitary, model?
The multiplicities NL,R must be chosen in such a way that the partition function is invariant under τ → τ + 1 and τ → −1/τ.

Another problem is related to the construction of various modular-invariant partition functions: What are the sets of representations – including representations based on both discrete and continuous series – which form a well-behaved OPA?

accepted.question_text: How can one define and compute meaningful characters or partition-function ingredients for non-compact SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten representations when the global representations are infinite-dimensional, the current-algebra modules have infinite degeneracy at each level, and no character formula is available for continuous-series representations?

evidence.quote: The unitary representations of the global algebra being infinite-dimensional, there is an infinite degeneracy level by level in the representations of the current algebra, and consequently the characters (2.3) are ill-defined.
this definition does not allow a regularization of the characters of the representations based on the continuous series.

One is the infinite degeneracy at each level in the representations of the current algebra, and in particular the treatment of the representations based on the continuous series for which no character formula has been proposed in the mathematical literature.

accepted.question_text: For string theory on the SU(1,1) group manifold, after coupling the SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten model to two-dimensional gravity and imposing Virasoro constraints, which left- and right-moving SU(1,1)L × SU(1,1)R current-algebra representations should be kept so that the string theory has a well-behaved operator algebra, positive-norm physical states, a clear role for discrete and continuous representations, and identifiable particle states with corresponding vertex operators?
accepted.context_brief: physical representations and vertex operators in the string spectrum

evidence.quote: The coupling of the above conformal model to the two-dimensional gravity creates spurious states that we should eliminate from the spectrum.

In this analysis, the natural questions are the following: What are the representations of the SU(1,1)L × SU(1,1)R current algebra that should be kept in order to have a consistent theory (in particular a well-behaved operator algebra)? What are the roles of discrete versus continuous representations? Are all physical states of positive norm? What kind of particles do these states describe, and what are the corresponding vertex operators?
there is no satisfactory selection of representations that can be performed, which guarantees the absence of negative-norm states in the physical Hilbert space.

accepted.question_text: For discrete highest-weight representations D−(j) in string theory on SU(1,1) at level k < −2, is imposing the spin bound k/2 ≤ j < 0 necessary and sufficient to remove all negative-norm physical states after Virasoro constraints, and can this be promoted to a genuine all-level no-ghost theorem?

evidence.quote: The mass-shell condition implies that this representation is present as long as j ≤ −1 (remember k < −2). In that range, unitarity thus demands k/2 ≤ j < 0.
Finally, the question to be answered is still whether the above condition (3.3) can indeed help to restore unitarity.
It is even more puzzling that a real no-ghost theorem might exist, based on the above observations and more specifically on the constraint (3.3) over the spin of the allowed discrete representations.

accepted.question_text: Can the proposed spin or mass cutoff k/2 ≤ j < 0, which may restore unitarity but removes the usual infinite tower of string excitations and gives a finite upper bound on the string level, be reconciled with the expected structure of string theory and with modular invariance of one-loop amplitudes?
accepted.context_brief: spin cutoff versus string spectrum and modular invariance

evidence.quote: It is important to be aware that this latter possibility violates the generic structure of the string spectrum itself. We lose the infinite tower of string modes (the mass is cut off at the scale of the radius of ADS3), and consequently the hope of constructing a consistent spectrum shrinks. Modular invariance is expected to be spoiled.
As was already stressed, the consistency of a string with a finite number of mass levels is questionable. One can in particular wonder what the issue of modular invariance could be.
Once more, compatibility between unitarity and modular invariance appears as an important issue in understanding the string propagating over ADS3.

accepted.question_text: Can a less formal treatment of string theory on AdS3—using the classical SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten model, classical string motion, a path-integral formulation, and explicit target-space boundary conditions—recover the physically expected states with j < k/2 that are cut off by the current-algebra analysis, clarify the role of continuous-series representations, and reveal whether boundary conditions create quantization ambiguities for strings analogous to those for particles on AdS3?

evidence.quote: we should get a better understanding of the SU(1,1) WZW model at the classical level, explore the classical motion of a string, and maybe try to follow a path-integral approach à la Gawȩdzki.
This implies in particular a proper treatment of the target-space boundary conditions that are hard to implement within the current-algebra method.
They might play a role in reconciling unitarity with the appearance of states of the discrete series with spin j < k/2, i.e. with mass above the anti-de Sitter radius scale.
The role of continuous series could also be clarified.
one should wonder whether target-space boundary conditions introduce ambiguities in the quantization of a string, similar to those appearing when solving the wave equation for a quantum particle.

accepted.question_text: Can modifications of the affine Sugawara construction or of the SU(1,1) current algebra avoid the mass/spin cutoff and the conclusion that continuous representations describe only tachyonic excitations, while still describing the original string theory on AdS3 and also addressing infinite level degeneracy and modular invariance?
accepted.context_brief: modified current algebra or Sugawara construction

evidence.quote: Alternatively, we might also need a deformation of the affine Sugawara construction in order to lift the degeneracy without coupling to an external field. Modification of the current algebra itself has also been advocated.
The question then arises whether these deformations still describe the initial WZW theory.

one could try alternatively to avoid the mass/spin cut-off and the purely tachyonic continuous representations in various ways, playing essentially with the current algebra, and/or modifying the affine Sugawara construction.
it is not clear whether such modifications leave unaltered the interpretation of the theory as a string propagating over ADS3.
none of the available attempts treats the problem of the infinite degeneracy at each string level, or enlightens the issue of modular invariance.

accepted.question_text: What is the physical and modular meaning of the source or magnetic field v coupled to J3_0 in SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten characters, and can it be interpreted as a continuous twist whose summation restores modular invariance in analogy with parafermionic constructions or the two-dimensional Euclidean black hole?

evidence.quote: In our formal treatment, the only way out is to lift the degeneracy by switching on a source coupled to J3_0.
the above models are only defined in the presence of a ‘magnetic field’, which is not invariant under modular transformations. The interpretation of these features is not clear.

In particular, the role of the ‘magnetic field’ v remains obscure. The possibility of interpreting it as a continuous twist, similar to those that appear in the parafermionic constructions, has never been exploited.
One might, though, relax in this way the constraint of modular invariance: the latter should be recovered only after an appropriate summation over v.

accepted.question_text: If negative-norm physical states are admitted in string theory on AdS3, can they be interpreted consistently by identifying the instability they represent and its physical origin in the AdS3 background, and can the known non-unitary models based on admissible SU(1,1) current-algebra representations be understood within string theory?

evidence.quote: a somewhat more exotic attitude with respect to the unitarity could be to simply admit the presence of negative-norm states in the physical spectrum, and then try to interpret them or, better, to identify the instability they are related to and its physical origin within the ADS3 background.

Following this line of thought, one could even reconsider the – non-unitary – models based on the admissible representations of the SU(1,1) current algebra; their partition function is known, and one should then try to understand them in the framework of string theory.

accepted.question_text: How can string theory be formulated for three-dimensional AdS-related black-hole backgrounds and for AdS3 backgrounds coupled to non-perturbative Ramond–Ramond charges rather than NS–NS torsion, especially in connection with black-hole evaporation?
accepted.context_brief: AdS3 black holes and Ramond–Ramond backgrounds

evidence.quote: Other peculiar features of ADS3 are the absence of asymptotically flat regions, the presence of boundaries (when conformally compactified), as well as a rich causal structure, which makes it possible to obtain three-dimensional black holes after modding out some discrete symmetry.
They include the string motion in a three-dimensional black hole, which settles the proper framework to address the black-hole evaporation problem.
Instead of a NS–NS torsion background, coupling to non-perturbative R–R charges is also a relevant and difficult problem.

accepted.question_text: For string theories on higher-dimensional anti-de Sitter spaces AdSn, how can exact conformal sigma models or conformal field theories be constructed and analyzed, including their spectra and interactions, when odd-dimensional cases require additional antisymmetric-tensor and linear-dilaton backgrounds and even-dimensional exact conformal field theories have not been investigated?

evidence.quote: string theories on more general ADSn backgrounds are equally important and more difficult than the three-dimensional case at hand.

In odd dimensions, it has been realized very recently that both an antisymmetric tensor and a linear dilaton are needed together with the gravitational background, in order to define an exactly conformal sigma model describing the string.
This sigma model is not a WZW model, and its spectrum and interactions remain quite unexplored.
the exact conformal field theories describing the string propagation on even-dimensional anti-de Sitter spaces have never been investigated.

accepted.question_text: Why, if at all, is the path-integral partition function obtained for Euclidean three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space H3+ = SL(2,C)/SU(2) satisfactory when it is not modular invariant, and what does that imply for the analogous SU(1,1) or AdS3 string-theory partition function?
accepted.context_brief: Euclidean H3+ partition function and modular invariance

evidence.quote: the result (2.10) was obtained in [6] as the partition function of Euclidean three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, H3+ ≡ SL(2,C)/SU(2), by using a rigorous path-integral approach.
It is not clear why such a non-modular-invariant partition function would be satisfactory in the case of H3+.
modular invariance should be demanded for any finite value of v.

accepted.question_text: Can SU(1,1) current-algebra representations without highest or lowest weight be given a stable string-theoretic interpretation in string theory on AdS3?

evidence.quote: Highest-weight representations of the SU(1,1) current algebra are labelled by the spin j of the primary fields.
Representations without highest or lowest weight do exist. It is, however, not clear how those could be interpreted within a stable string theory.
